title: RTX 5070 vs RX 9070 XT (2026): Which 1440p GPU Should You Buy?
description: The RX 9070 XT is the better 1440p buy for most: 16 GB vs 12 GB and faster raster for $50 to $80 more. The RTX 5070 wins on DLSS 4, ray tracing and power.
quick: Pick the RTX 5070 if you want the lower price, a 250 W card that runs on a 650 W PSU, and the widest support for DLSS 4 and multi frame generation. Pick the RX 9070 XT if you play at 1440p with high texture settings and want 16 GB of VRAM, plus noticeably faster raster performance that independent reviews put close to an RTX 5070 Ti.
differ: Is 12 GB of VRAM enough at 1440p?

For now, mostly yes, but it is the RTX 5070's weak spot. A handful of recent games at 1440p with ultra textures and ray tracing push past 12 GB, and when a card runs out of video memory you get stutter rather than a smooth drop in frame rate. The RX 9070 XT carries 16 GB on a 256-bit bus, which leaves room for texture packs and mods and makes it the safer card to keep for four or five years. If you lower textures one notch, 12 GB is fine in nearly everything today.
How much faster is the RX 9070 XT?

In traditional raster games, independent reviews generally put the RX 9070 XT about 15 to 20 percent ahead of the RTX 5070 at 1440p, close to the more expensive RTX 5070 Ti. The gap narrows with heavy ray tracing, where NVIDIA's RT hardware holds up better, and it can flip in path-traced titles. For the typical mix of shooters, racing and open-world games without path tracing, the AMD card is the quicker of the two.
Which upscaler is better, DLSS 4 or FSR 4?

DLSS 4 is still the safer bet because it is in far more games, and NVIDIA's multi frame generation can multiply displayed frames on top of that. FSR 4 closed most of the image-quality gap with machine-learning upscaling, and owners report it looks much better than FSR 3. The catch is the game list: FSR 4 support is growing but smaller. If your favorite games already list FSR 4, the difference is small. If not, DLSS gives the RTX 5070 a real edge.
What about power and the PSU?

The RTX 5070 is rated at 250 W and NVIDIA recommends a 650 W power supply. The RX 9070 XT is rated at 304 W, and many partner cards run higher, so a quality 750 W unit is the comfortable choice. Most RX 9070 XT models use standard 8-pin connectors, while the RTX 5070 uses 12V-2x6 or an adapter. If your current PSU is a 650 W Gold unit, the RTX 5070 is the drop-in option.
buyA: You want a 1440p card under about $650 that works with a 650 W power supply
Your games support DLSS 4 and you plan to use frame generation
You play ray-traced or path-traced titles and want NVIDIA's RT performance
buyB: You want 16 GB of VRAM for ultra textures and a longer upgrade cycle
You play mostly raster games and want the most frames per dollar at 1440p
You prefer standard 8-pin power connectors over 12V-2x6

faqs.q: Is the RX 9070 XT worth the extra money over the RTX 5070?
faqs.a: Yes, for most 1440p players. The extra $50 to $80 buys 4 GB more VRAM and roughly 15 to 20 percent more raster performance in independent reviews. The RTX 5070 makes more sense if your budget is fixed or your PSU is 650 W.

faqs.q: Can a 650 W PSU run the RX 9070 XT?
faqs.a: It can with some reference-clocked cards and an efficient CPU, but 750 W is the safer pick. AMD rates the card at 304 W, and factory-overclocked models draw more during spikes.

faqs.q: Which card is better for streaming on Twitch or YouTube?
faqs.a: Both have good hardware encoders now. NVIDIA's NVENC has the longer track record and wider app support, while AMD improved its encoder a lot with RDNA 4. For most streamers either works.

title: RTX 5070 vs RX 9070 (2026): 12 GB or 16 GB for 1440p Gaming?
description: The RX 9070 edges the RTX 5070 for 1440p: 16 GB of VRAM, 220 W and slightly faster raster at a similar $550 to $650. Pick NVIDIA for DLSS 4 and ray tracing.
quick: Pick the RTX 5070 if you lean on DLSS 4, play ray-traced games often, or want NVIDIA's multi frame generation. Pick the RX 9070 if you care more about VRAM and efficiency: it has 16 GB versus 12 GB, a 220 W rating versus 250 W, and independent reviews show it slightly ahead in raster games at about the same street price.
differ: Which one is faster in normal games?

In raster workloads, independent reviews generally show the RX 9070 a few percent to about 10 percent ahead of the RTX 5070 at 1440p, depending on the game list. That is close enough that you would struggle to notice it without a frame counter. Turn on heavy ray tracing and the order often reverses, with the RTX 5070 pulling ahead. Treat these two as performance twins and decide on memory, features and price.
Does the 4 GB VRAM difference matter?

It matters more the longer you keep the card. The RX 9070 has 16 GB on a 256-bit bus, while the RTX 5070 has 12 GB on a 192-bit bus with faster GDDR7. Today, 12 GB covers almost every game at 1440p with sensible settings. A few demanding releases already exceed it at maximum textures. If you buy a card every two years, ignore this. If you keep one for five, the extra headroom is worth having.
Which is more efficient?

AMD rates the RX 9070 at 220 W and NVIDIA rates the RTX 5070 at 250 W. That 30 W gap is small on a power bill, but it lets the RX 9070 run cooler and quieter in compact cases, and many partner models are short two-fan designs. Both cards are fine on a quality 650 W power supply. The RX 9070 typically uses 8-pin connectors, while the RTX 5070 uses 12V-2x6 or an adapter.
How do the software features compare?

NVIDIA's advantage is breadth: DLSS 4 upscaling and multi frame generation are in hundreds of games, plus Reflex for lower latency and a mature NVENC encoder. AMD's FSR 4 upscaling is a big step up in image quality, but fewer games support it so far. AMD's Adrenalin driver suite is well regarded and includes frame generation and performance overlays. If a specific game you play only supports DLSS, that should decide it.
buyA: Your favorite games support DLSS 4 and you want multi frame generation
You play path-traced or heavy ray-traced games
You stream or edit video and want NVENC with the widest app support
buyB: You keep cards for years and want 16 GB of VRAM
You want the lower 220 W rating for a small or quiet build
You mostly play raster games and want slightly more speed for the money

faqs.q: Is the RX 9070 or RTX 5070 better for a small form factor PC?
faqs.a: The RX 9070 has the edge. Its 220 W rating is 30 W lower, and many partner cards are compact two-fan models. Check card length against your case either way.

faqs.q: Should I spend more for the RX 9070 XT instead?
faqs.a: If the gap is under about $80, yes. The RX 9070 XT is roughly 10 to 15 percent faster in independent reviews but draws 304 W, so plan on a 750 W PSU.

title: RTX 5070 Ti vs RX 9070 XT (2026): Is NVIDIA Worth $150 More?
description: The RX 9070 XT matches the RTX 5070 Ti in most raster games for about $150 less, and both have 16 GB. Pay up for the 5070 Ti only for ray tracing and DLSS 4.
quick: Pick the RTX 5070 Ti if you play ray-traced and path-traced games, want DLSS 4 with multi frame generation, or care about lower power at a given frame rate. Pick the RX 9070 XT if you mostly play raster games: independent reviews put it within a few percent of the 5070 Ti there, both have 16 GB, and the AMD card usually costs $120 to $170 less.
differ: How close are they in raster games?

Very close. Independent reviews at 1440p and 4K generally show the RX 9070 XT trailing the RTX 5070 Ti by a low single-digit percentage on average, with individual games going either way. Both have 16 GB of VRAM on a 256-bit bus, so neither runs short of memory in current games. If you play mostly esports, racing and open-world titles without heavy ray tracing, the cheaper card gives you nearly the same experience.
Where does the RTX 5070 Ti pull ahead?

Ray tracing is the main split. With RT effects turned up, and especially with path tracing, the RTX 5070 Ti holds a clear lead in independent reviews. NVIDIA's software stack adds to it: DLSS 4 is supported in far more games than FSR 4, and multi frame generation can raise displayed frame rates for high-refresh monitors. For 4K with RT on, the NVIDIA card is the better tool.
Which draws more power?

NVIDIA rates the RTX 5070 Ti at 300 W, and AMD rates the RX 9070 XT at 304 W, but many partner 9070 XT models ship with higher factory limits. In practice the RTX 5070 Ti tends to deliver more frames per watt. NVIDIA recommends a 750 W PSU, which is also a sensible floor for the 9070 XT. The 5070 Ti uses 12V-2x6, while most 9070 XT cards use two or three 8-pin plugs.
Is the price gap worth it?

That depends on how you play. At typical street prices the RTX 5070 Ti costs $750 to $900 and the RX 9070 XT $600 to $730, a difference of roughly 20 percent for very similar raster performance. If RT and DLSS are central to your games, the 5070 Ti is worth the premium. If they are not, the money is better spent on a faster CPU, more storage or a better monitor.
buyA: You play path-traced or ray-traced games at 1440p or 4K
You want DLSS 4 and multi frame generation in the widest list of games
You want better performance per watt and a 12V-2x6 single-cable setup
buyB: You want 5070 Ti-class raster performance for about $150 less
You prefer 8-pin power connectors and your PSU lacks 12V-2x6
You care more about frames per dollar than about ray tracing

faqs.q: Which is better for 4K gaming, the RTX 5070 Ti or RX 9070 XT?
faqs.a: Both handle 4K with upscaling. The RTX 5070 Ti is the better 4K card if you use ray tracing, thanks to stronger RT hardware and DLSS 4. Without RT, they are close.

faqs.q: Do both cards need a 750 W power supply?
faqs.a: NVIDIA recommends 750 W for the RTX 5070 Ti, and 750 W is the sensible floor for the RX 9070 XT, whose partner cards often run above AMD's 304 W rating.

title: RTX 5060 Ti 16GB vs RX 9060 XT 16GB (2026): Best $400 GPU?
description: The RX 9060 XT 16GB is the better value: same 16 GB and close raster speed for $50 to $80 less. The RTX 5060 Ti 16GB wins on ray tracing and DLSS 4.
quick: Pick the RTX 5060 Ti 16GB if you want stronger ray tracing, DLSS 4 support in more games and a 180 W card with excellent efficiency. Pick the RX 9060 XT 16GB if you want the most performance per dollar, or if your motherboard runs PCIe 3.0: AMD's card uses a full x16 link, while the 5060 Ti uses x8.
differ: Which card is faster?

In raster games, independent reviews generally show the RTX 5060 Ti 16GB slightly ahead of the RX 9060 XT 16GB, by single digits on average at 1080p and 1440p. With ray tracing on, NVIDIA's lead grows. Both cards have 16 GB on a 128-bit bus, so memory capacity is a tie. The question is whether a modest speed bump and better RT are worth the extra $50 to $80 at current street prices.
Does PCIe 3.0 matter for these cards?

It can. The RTX 5060 Ti uses a PCIe 5.0 x8 connection. On a PCIe 4.0 or 5.0 board that is plenty, but on an older PCIe 3.0 board, such as a B450 system, the card gets half the bandwidth it was designed for, and some games lose a few percent. The RX 9060 XT uses all 16 lanes, so it holds up better on older platforms. If you are upgrading a Ryzen 5 2600 or similar system, the AMD card is the safer pick.
How do DLSS 4 and FSR 4 compare here?

Upscaling matters more on midrange cards because you lean on it to hit high refresh rates at 1440p. DLSS 4 is in far more games and includes multi frame generation. FSR 4 delivers much better image quality than older FSR versions, but its game list is shorter. If you play new AAA releases that ship with DLSS on day one, the RTX 5060 Ti has the practical edge.
What about power and noise?

NVIDIA rates the RTX 5060 Ti 16GB at 180 W. AMD's RX 9060 XT 16GB lands around 160 to 180 W depending on the partner card. Both run comfortably on a 550 W to 650 W power supply and both come in compact two-fan designs. In practice neither card is loud or hard to cool, so this is close to a tie. Either card runs on a 650 W to 750 W unit; see our [best PSU for RTX 5060 Ti](/best-psu-for-rtx-5060-ti/) guide.
buyA: You want better ray tracing and DLSS 4 in more games
Your board is PCIe 4.0 or newer, so the x8 link costs nothing
You stream and want NVIDIA's NVENC encoder
buyB: You want 16 GB at the lowest price, around $350 to $400
You are upgrading an older PCIe 3.0 system
You mostly play raster games and prefer to save the difference

faqs.q: Is the 8 GB version of either card worth buying instead?
faqs.a: Not for most people in 2026. Both 8 GB versions run short of memory in several new games at 1080p high settings. The 16 GB versions cost more but avoid that problem.

faqs.q: Which card is better for a Ryzen 5 3600 on a B450 board?
faqs.a: The RX 9060 XT 16GB. B450 runs the GPU slot at PCIe 3.0, and the AMD card's full x16 link loses less bandwidth than the RTX 5060 Ti's x8 link.

title: RTX 5060 vs Arc B580 (2026): Best GPU Around $300?
description: The RTX 5060 is the safer pick for most at $300 to $330: faster in most games and no CPU-overhead issue. The Arc B580 offers 12 GB of VRAM for about $40 less.
quick: Pick the RTX 5060 if you have an older or midrange CPU, want consistent performance across all games and want DLSS 4 support. Pick the Arc B580 if you have a modern CPU, a board with Resizable BAR enabled, and value 12 GB of VRAM over 8 GB. It is cheaper and handles high textures better, but its driver overhead punishes older processors.
differ: Is 8 GB on the RTX 5060 a problem?

It is the biggest compromise on this card. Several 2025 and 2026 games exceed 8 GB at 1080p with high or ultra textures, which causes stutter or texture pop-in. You can avoid it by lowering texture quality, and most esports titles never come close. The Arc B580 has 12 GB on a 192-bit bus, which gives it more room in new AAA games. If you mainly play those, the extra memory counts for a lot at this price.
What is the Arc B580 CPU overhead issue?

Independent reviews found that the Arc B580 loses noticeably more performance than NVIDIA or AMD cards when paired with older CPUs like the Ryzen 5 2600 or 3600. Intel's driver uses more CPU time per frame, so a slower processor becomes a bottleneck sooner. On a modern chip such as a Ryzen 5 7600 the card performs as intended. On an older system, the RTX 5060 is the more predictable choice.
Which is faster overall?

With a fast CPU, independent reviews generally show the RTX 5060 ahead of the Arc B580 in most games at 1080p, with the B580 closing the gap or winning when 8 GB runs out. With an older CPU, the RTX 5060's lead grows. NVIDIA's drivers are also more consistent across older DirectX 11 titles, where Intel has improved but still has rough spots in some games.
Are there platform requirements?

Yes, for the Arc B580. Intel says the card needs Resizable BAR enabled, and performance drops sharply without it. Most boards from the last several years support it after a BIOS update, but very old platforms do not. Both cards use an x8 PCIe link, PCIe 4.0 on the B580 and PCIe 5.0 on the RTX 5060, so both lose a little on PCIe 3.0 boards. The B580 is rated at 190 W versus 145 W.
buyA: You have an older CPU such as a Ryzen 5 3600 or Core i5-10400
You want DLSS 4 and consistent drivers across older games
You want a lower 145 W rating for a small case or modest PSU
buyB: You have a modern CPU and Resizable BAR enabled
You want 12 GB of VRAM for new games at 1080p and 1440p
You want the lowest price, around $250 to $290

faqs.q: Does the Arc B580 work without Resizable BAR?
faqs.a: It works, but Intel requires Resizable BAR for full performance and frame rates drop a lot without it. Check that your BIOS has it enabled before buying.

faqs.q: Which card is better for 1440p, the RTX 5060 or Arc B580?
faqs.a: Neither is a true 1440p card, but the Arc B580's 12 GB holds up better there in newer games, provided your CPU is modern. The RTX 5060 needs lower textures at 1440p.

title: RTX 5080 vs RTX 5070 Ti (2026): Is the 5080 Worth $300 More?
description: The RTX 5070 Ti is the better value: same 16 GB and about 85% of the RTX 5080's speed for $250 to $400 less. Buy the 5080 only for high-refresh 4K with RT on.
quick: Pick the RTX 5080 if you game at 4K with ray tracing on and want the fastest card short of the RTX 5090, with about 15 percent more performance than the 5070 Ti in independent reviews. Pick the RTX 5070 Ti if you play at 1440p or 4K with upscaling and want nearly the same experience, the same 16 GB of VRAM and a lower 300 W rating for much less money.
differ: How much faster is the RTX 5080?

Independent reviews generally put the RTX 5080 around 15 percent ahead of the RTX 5070 Ti, a bit more at 4K and a bit less at 1440p. That follows the specs: 10,752 CUDA cores against 8,960, both on a 256-bit GDDR7 bus. The two cards share the same GPU die family, so features are identical. You are paying for extra shader cores and higher clocks, not for a different class of card.
Do they have the same VRAM?

Yes. Both carry 16 GB of GDDR7 on a 256-bit bus, which is plenty for 1440p and enough for 4K in nearly all current games. That is the main reason the RTX 5070 Ti is such good value: it has no memory disadvantage. If you wanted more than 16 GB for 4K texture packs, local AI models or heavy creative work, the next step is the 32 GB RTX 5090, not the 5080.
What PSU does each card need?

NVIDIA rates the RTX 5080 at 360 W and recommends an 850 W power supply. The RTX 5070 Ti is rated at 300 W with a 750 W recommendation. Both use the 12V-2x6 connector, so an ATX 3.1 unit with a native cable is the cleanest setup. If you already own a quality 750 W unit, the 5070 Ti avoids a PSU upgrade, which widens its value lead even further.
Which is the better long-term buy?

For most people, the RTX 5070 Ti. With identical features and memory, the 5080's extra 15 percent will matter less over time than the $250 to $400 you save, which can go toward a CPU or monitor upgrade. The RTX 5080 makes sense if you own a 4K 144 Hz or faster display and want the highest native frame rates without stepping up to the RTX 5090's price.
buyA: You play at 4K with ray tracing and want maximum native frame rates
You own a 4K high-refresh monitor and the RTX 5090 is out of budget
You already have an 850 W ATX 3.1 power supply
buyB: You want the same 16 GB and features for $250 to $400 less
You play at 1440p, where the gap shrinks
You have a 750 W power supply and want to keep it

faqs.q: Can you overclock the RTX 5070 Ti to RTX 5080 speeds?
faqs.a: No. Overclocking adds a few percent, but the RTX 5080 has about 20 percent more CUDA cores. An overclocked 5070 Ti narrows the gap without closing it.

faqs.q: Is 16 GB enough for 4K on these cards?
faqs.a: Yes, in nearly all current games. A few titles with maximum textures and path tracing approach the limit, but both cards handle 4K with upscaling without running out.

title: RTX 5090 vs RTX 5080 (2026): Is Double the Price Worth It?
description: The RTX 5090 is the fastest gaming GPU, about 50% quicker than the RTX 5080 at 4K with 32 GB of VRAM, but costs about twice as much and draws 575 W vs 360 W.
quick: Pick the RTX 5090 if you game at 4K or above with path tracing, run local AI models or render heavy 3D scenes, and need 32 GB of VRAM. Pick the RTX 5080 if you want excellent 4K and 1440p gaming for about half the price, with a 360 W rating and an 850 W PSU instead of the 5090's 575 W and 1,000 W recommendation.
differ: How big is the performance gap?

The specs are lopsided: the RTX 5090 has 21,760 CUDA cores on a 512-bit bus, against 10,752 cores on a 256-bit bus for the RTX 5080. Independent reviews show the 5090 around 50 percent faster at 4K in many games, with a smaller lead at 1440p where the CPU starts to hold it back. At 1080p, the 5090 is often CPU-limited and its advantage shrinks a lot.
Who actually needs 32 GB of VRAM?

Gamers rarely do. 16 GB on the RTX 5080 covers current games at 4K. The 32 GB on the RTX 5090 matters for creators and AI users: large language models running locally, 3D rendering with big scenes, and 8K video timelines. If any of that is part of your work, the 5090's memory can be the reason to buy it on its own, because models that do not fit in VRAM slow down dramatically.
What does the RTX 5090 demand from the rest of the PC?

A lot. NVIDIA rates it at 575 W and recommends a 1,000 W power supply, ideally ATX 3.1 with a native 12V-2x6 cable seated fully. Many partner cards are large, so check case length and width. You also need a fast CPU such as a Ryzen 7 9800X3D to avoid a bottleneck. The RTX 5080, at 360 W and 850 W recommended, fits into far more existing builds.
Is the RTX 5090 good value?

Not by frames per dollar. At $2,000 to $2,700 against $1,000 to $1,300, you pay roughly twice as much for about 50 percent more 4K performance. The 5090 makes sense if you need the fastest card available, use its 32 GB professionally, or play at 4K 240 Hz. For everyone else, the RTX 5080 is the more balanced high-end choice.
buyA: You play at 4K high refresh or above with path tracing on
You run local AI models or large 3D scenes that need 32 GB of VRAM
You have, or will buy, a 1,000 W ATX 3.1 power supply
buyB: You want strong 4K gaming for roughly half the price
You play at 1440p, where the RTX 5090's lead shrinks
Your PSU is 850 W and you do not want to replace it

faqs.q: Is the RTX 5090 overkill for 1440p?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. At 1440p the CPU often limits frame rates before the RTX 5090 does, so its lead over the RTX 5080 shrinks. It makes most sense at 4K and above.

faqs.q: Is the 12V-2x6 connector on the RTX 5090 safe?
faqs.a: It is safe when seated fully, with no sharp bend near the plug. Use a native cable from an ATX 3.1 PSU rather than an adapter, and check the connector clicks in.

faqs.q: Will an 850 W PSU run the RTX 5090?
faqs.a: NVIDIA recommends 1,000 W. An excellent 850 W unit can work with a modest CPU, but you lose headroom for power spikes. Plan on 1,000 W for a 5090 build.

title: RTX 5060 vs RX 9060 XT 16GB (2026): Is 8 GB Still Enough?
description: The RX 9060 XT 16GB is worth $50 to $70 more than the RTX 5060: double the VRAM, a full x16 link and similar or better speed. The 5060 suits esports builds.
quick: Pick the RTX 5060 if you play esports titles at 1080p, want DLSS 4 and need to keep the card near $300. Pick the RX 9060 XT 16GB if you play new AAA games, want twice the VRAM so texture settings are not a constant trade-off, or are upgrading an older PCIe 3.0 system where its full x16 link holds up better.
differ: Why does 16 GB versus 8 GB matter so much?

VRAM shortfalls do not show up as a modest drop in frame rate. They show up as stutter, blurry textures that never load and sometimes crashes. A growing list of new games use more than 8 GB at 1080p with high textures. The RX 9060 XT 16GB never hits that wall at this tier, while the RTX 5060 needs medium textures in those games. For Valorant, CS2 or Fortnite, 8 GB is still fine.
Which card is faster?

When memory is not the limit, the two are close, and independent reviews show the RX 9060 XT 16GB slightly ahead in raster games on average. When a game exceeds 8 GB, the AMD card can be far ahead. NVIDIA keeps an edge in ray tracing and in DLSS game support. In short, the 5060 holds its own in lighter games and falls behind as settings and resolution climb.
How do they handle older motherboards?

This favors AMD. The RTX 5060 uses a PCIe 5.0 x8 link, which drops to x8 at PCIe 3.0 speed on older boards like B450. That costs a few percent, and more when VRAM spills over the bus. The RX 9060 XT uses a full x16 link, so it keeps twice the bandwidth on the same old board. For Ryzen 2000 and 3000 upgrades, that is a practical advantage.
What about power?

NVIDIA rates the RTX 5060 at 145 W. The RX 9060 XT 16GB lands around 160 to 180 W, depending on the partner card. Both run easily on a 550 W power supply, and both come in short two-fan versions for small cases. The RTX 5060 is slightly more efficient, but not by enough to change the decision for most builds.
buyA: You mostly play esports titles at 1080p
Your budget stops near $300 to $330
You want DLSS 4 and the lowest power draw
buyB: You play new AAA games and want 16 GB of VRAM
You are upgrading a PCIe 3.0 board such as B450
You plan to keep the card three years or more

faqs.q: Is the RTX 5060 good enough for 1080p in 2026?
faqs.a: Yes for esports and older games, and for new AAA games with textures set to medium. Its 8 GB of VRAM is the limit, not the GPU's raw speed.

faqs.q: Should I buy the RX 9060 XT 8GB to save money?
faqs.a: Most buyers should not. The 8 GB version has the same memory limit as the RTX 5060. The 16 GB version costs more but avoids the stutter in demanding games.

title: RX 9070 vs RX 9070 XT (2026): Is the XT Worth the Extra Cost?
description: The RX 9070 XT is about 10 to 15% faster than the RX 9070 for $50 to $110 more, and both have 16 GB. The 9070 draws 220 W vs 304 W and is easier to cool.
quick: Pick the RX 9070 if you want 16 GB at 1440p with a lower 220 W rating, a smaller card and a 650 W power supply. Pick the RX 9070 XT if the price gap is small: it has 64 compute units versus 56, higher clocks and roughly 10 to 15 percent more performance in independent reviews, but it draws 304 W and runs best on a 750 W unit.
differ: What is actually different between them?

Both use the same RDNA 4 chip with 16 GB of GDDR6 on a 256-bit bus. The RX 9070 XT enables 64 compute units, or 4,096 stream processors, and runs higher clocks. The RX 9070 has 56 compute units, or 3,584 stream processors, and a much lower power limit. Features, including FSR 4, AV1 encoding and ray tracing hardware, are the same. It is a straight speed-for-power trade.
How much faster is the XT?

Independent reviews generally put the RX 9070 XT about 10 to 15 percent ahead at 1440p and 4K. That is the difference between, for example, holding a steady 144 Hz and dipping below it in demanding games. If the price gap is $50, that is good value. If it stretches past $100, the RX 9070 becomes the better buy, because the extra money could go to a faster CPU or more storage.
Which is easier to power and cool?

The RX 9070. AMD rates it at 220 W, compared with 304 W for the XT, and many 9070 XT partner cards ship with even higher limits. The RX 9070 runs on a quality 650 W PSU, often with two 8-pin connectors, and partner coolers can be shorter and quieter. The XT is more likely to need a 750 W unit and a case with good airflow for a triple-fan card.
Can you tune the RX 9070 closer to the XT?

Partly. Owners report that the RX 9070 responds well to raising the power limit and undervolting in AMD's Adrenalin software, which can close some of the gap. It cannot add the missing compute units, so the XT stays ahead. Treat any tuning gains as a bonus, and buy based on stock performance and the street prices you see on the day.
buyA: You want 16 GB at 1440p with a 220 W rating
Your PSU is 650 W or your case is compact
The XT costs more than about $100 extra
buyB: The price gap is around $50 to $80
You want roughly 10 to 15 percent more frames at 1440p or 4K
You have a 750 W PSU and a case with good airflow

faqs.q: Do the RX 9070 and RX 9070 XT support FSR 4?
faqs.a: Yes. Both cards use RDNA 4 and support FSR 4's machine-learning upscaling, along with the same ray tracing and encoding hardware.

faqs.q: Is the RX 9070 good for 4K?
faqs.a: It handles 4K with FSR upscaling in most games. Its 16 GB of VRAM is enough, but the RX 9070 XT or an NVIDIA RTX 5070 Ti gives more headroom at native 4K.

title: Arc B580 vs RX 9060 XT 16GB (2026): Best Budget GPU Pick?
description: The RX 9060 XT 16GB is the stronger card: faster, 16 GB vs 12 GB, and no CPU-overhead penalty for $80 to $120 more. The Arc B580 wins on price alone.
quick: Pick the Arc B580 if your budget tops out around $250 to $290, you have a modern CPU, and Resizable BAR is enabled. Pick the RX 9060 XT 16GB if you can stretch to $350 to $400: independent reviews show it clearly faster, it has 16 GB instead of 12 GB, and it does not lose performance on older CPUs the way the B580 does.
differ: How much faster is the RX 9060 XT 16GB?

Independent reviews generally show the RX 9060 XT 16GB clearly ahead of the Arc B580 at 1080p and 1440p, with the margin growing in newer games and with ray tracing on. The AMD card has 32 compute units on RDNA 4 against the B580's 20 Xe2 cores. You pay roughly 30 to 40 percent more for it, and in many games the performance gap is in the same range.
Does your CPU change the answer?

Yes, a lot. The Arc B580 has widely reported driver overhead, so with older CPUs like the Ryzen 5 2600 or 3600 it loses much more performance than the RX 9060 XT does. If you are upgrading an older system, the AMD card is the clear choice. With a modern CPU such as a Ryzen 5 7600 or Core Ultra 5 245K, the B580 performs as intended and the value case for it is much stronger.
Is 12 GB enough, or do you need 16 GB?

12 GB on the B580 is comfortable for 1080p today and workable at 1440p with sensible texture settings. 16 GB on the RX 9060 XT gives more headroom for maximum textures and future releases. Both are a real step up from 8 GB cards. If you keep cards a long time, the extra 4 GB is useful, but 12 GB is not the problem 8 GB has become.
How do platform needs compare?

The Arc B580 needs Resizable BAR enabled for full performance and uses a PCIe 4.0 x8 link, which loses some bandwidth on PCIe 3.0 boards. The RX 9060 XT uses a full PCIe 5.0 x16 link and is less sensitive to older slots. The B580 is rated at 190 W and the RX 9060 XT at about 160 to 180 W. Both run on a 550 W power supply.

faqs.q: Is the Arc B580 still a good buy in 2026?
faqs.a: It is a good buy with a modern CPU and Resizable BAR on, at around $250 to $290. With an older CPU, an RX 9060 XT or RTX 5060 is the safer choice.

faqs.q: Which is better for a PCIe 3.0 motherboard?
faqs.a: The RX 9060 XT 16GB. It uses a full x16 link, while the Arc B580 uses x8 at PCIe 4.0 speed, which halves to PCIe 3.0 x8 bandwidth on older boards.

title: Ryzen 7 9800X3D vs 7800X3D (2026): Is the Upgrade Worth It?
description: The Ryzen 7 9800X3D is about 8 to 10% faster in games than the 7800X3D in reviews, and much stronger in multi-core work. The 7800X3D costs roughly $60 less.
quick: Pick the Ryzen 7 9800X3D if you are building new, want the fastest gaming CPU on AM5 and also do some streaming, encoding or compiling. Pick the Ryzen 7 7800X3D if you find it at a clear discount: it has the same 8 cores and 96 MB of L3, and in games the gap is modest. Owners of a 7800X3D gain little by upgrading.
differ: How much faster is the 9800X3D in games?

Independent reviews generally put the Ryzen 7 9800X3D around 8 to 10 percent ahead of the 7800X3D on average at 1080p with a high-end GPU, with some games showing more. At 1440p and 4K, the GPU becomes the limit and the gap shrinks to low single digits. Both chips have 8 cores, 16 threads and 96 MB of L3 cache, so they are close cousins rather than different classes of CPU.
What changed with the cache placement?

On the 7800X3D, the extra cache sits on top of the CPU cores, which traps heat and forced AMD to cap clocks at 5.0 GHz and lock overclocking. On the 9800X3D, AMD moved the 3D V-Cache under the core die. The cores sit closer to the cooler, so the chip boosts to 5.2 GHz, sustains higher all-core clocks and allows overclocking. That is why the 9800X3D gains much more in multi-threaded work than in games.
How big is the multi-core difference?

Larger than the gaming gap. Thanks to Zen 5 cores and higher sustained clocks, the 9800X3D is noticeably quicker in rendering, code compiles and video encoding, with independent reviews showing roughly 15 to 25 percent gains in many multi-threaded tests. If your PC does double duty as a work machine or you stream while gaming, that extra performance is the stronger argument for the newer chip.
Should a 7800X3D owner upgrade?

Almost never. Both use the AM5 socket and the same 120 W TDP, so the swap is easy, but you would spend $450 or more for a modest gaming gain. A GPU upgrade will do far more for frame rates. The 9800X3D upgrade makes more sense for someone coming from a Ryzen 5 7600 or an older AM4 system, where the jump is large.

buyB: You find it at least $60 to $80 cheaper than the 9800X3D
You play at 1440p or 4K, where the gap shrinks
You want 96 MB of 3D V-Cache on a tighter budget

faqs.q: Do the 9800X3D and 7800X3D need the same cooler?
faqs.a: Yes, a good dual-tower air cooler handles either one. Both are rated at 120 W. The 9800X3D can run warmer under full load because it boosts higher, so avoid budget single-fan coolers.

faqs.q: Can I overclock the Ryzen 7 9800X3D?
faqs.a: Yes. AMD unlocked overclocking on the 9800X3D because the cache now sits under the cores. The 7800X3D supports Curve Optimizer undervolting but not multiplier overclocking.

title: Ryzen 7 9800X3D vs Ryzen 9 9950X3D (2026): Gaming or Both?
description: For pure gaming the Ryzen 7 9800X3D matches the 9950X3D for about $200 less. The 9950X3D doubles the cores to 16 for rendering and compiling.
quick: Pick the Ryzen 7 9800X3D if your PC is mainly for games: it delivers the same class of gaming performance for $450 to $480 and is simpler to run. Pick the Ryzen 9 9950X3D if you also render video, compile large projects or run many virtual machines. It adds 8 more cores, a 5.7 GHz boost and 128 MB of L3 for top-tier gaming plus workstation multi-core speed.
differ: Is the 9950X3D faster in games?

Usually not by much. Independent reviews show the two within a few percent of each other in most games, with the 9800X3D sometimes ahead. The 9950X3D's 16 cores span two chiplets, and only one has the extra 3D V-Cache. For games, AMD's drivers steer threads to the cache chiplet. When that works, you get 9800X3D-like results. When it does not, you can lose a little performance.
How much faster is it for work?

A lot. The Ryzen 9 9950X3D has 16 cores and 32 threads against 8 and 16, so in rendering, compiling and video export it can finish heavy jobs close to twice as fast in well-threaded apps. If your income depends on Blender, Premiere, Unreal builds or similar, the 9950X3D pays for itself in time saved. For gaming plus light browsing and Discord, those extra cores sit idle.
What about power and cooling?

AMD rates the 9800X3D at 120 W and the 9950X3D at 170 W. A good dual-tower air cooler handles the 9800X3D comfortably. The 9950X3D also runs on high-end air, but sustained all-core work makes a 360 mm AIO or a top air cooler like the Noctua NH-D15 G2 more comfortable. Neither chip includes a cooler, so budget for one either way.
Does the 9950X3D need special setup?

A little. You should install AMD's chipset driver and keep Windows Game Mode on, so the scheduler sends games to the cache chiplet. Owners report it works well with current drivers. The 9800X3D has a single chiplet, so there is nothing to manage. If you want a plug-in-and-play gaming chip, the simpler design is an advantage of its own. Keep the BIOS current too.

faqs.a: No. Only one of the two chiplets has the extra cache. AMD's chipset driver and Windows Game Mode steer games onto that chiplet.

faqs.q: Is the 9950X3D worth it for streaming while gaming?
faqs.a: It helps if you encode on the CPU. Most streamers use the GPU's hardware encoder instead, which makes the 9800X3D's 8 cores plenty.

title: Ryzen 7 9800X3D vs Core Ultra 7 265K (2026): Best Gaming CPU?
description: The Ryzen 7 9800X3D is the far better gaming CPU, well ahead of the Core Ultra 7 265K in reviews. The 265K costs $150 to $200 less and has 20 cores.
quick: Pick the Ryzen 7 9800X3D if gaming is the priority: its 96 MB of L3 cache gives it a large lead in independent reviews, and AM5 has a longer upgrade path. Pick the Core Ultra 7 265K if you do as much productivity work as gaming and want 20 cores for $260 to $300, which makes it strong value for rendering and compiling on a budget.
differ: How big is the gaming gap?

Large. Independent reviews consistently show the Ryzen 7 9800X3D well ahead of the Core Ultra 7 265K at 1080p with a fast GPU, often by 20 percent or more on average, with bigger margins in cache-sensitive games like simulators and strategy titles. At 4K with a midrange GPU, the gap mostly disappears because the graphics card sets the limit. The more frames you want, the more the AMD chip matters.
Which is better for productivity?

The Core Ultra 7 265K has 20 cores, 8 performance and 12 efficiency, against 8 cores and 16 threads on the 9800X3D. In heavily threaded work like rendering and compiling, independent reviews show the Intel chip ahead, sometimes by a wide margin. For the price, it is one of the strongest multi-core CPUs available. If you edit video for a living and game occasionally, that changes the math.
What about the platform and upgrades?

AM5 has a clearer future. AMD has supported it since 2022 and has said it will keep supporting it through at least 2027, so a 9800X3D board may take another CPU generation. The Intel chip's lower price can buy a better motherboard, but expect to replace it at your next CPU upgrade.
How do power and cooling compare?

AMD rates the 9800X3D at 120 W. Intel lists the 265K at 125 W base and up to 250 W maximum turbo, and it can pull close to that in all-core workloads. In games both chips draw far less than their limits. A good dual-tower air cooler handles either. For long rendering sessions, the 265K benefits from a stronger cooler or a 360 mm AIO.

faqs.a: Neither includes a cooler. A $35 to $45 dual-tower air cooler such as the Thermalright Peerless Assassin 120 SE is a good match for either chip in gaming builds.

title: Ryzen 5 9600X vs Ryzen 5 7600 (2026): Is Zen 5 Worth It?
description: The Ryzen 5 7600 is the better value: within about 5% of the 9600X in games, $20 to $30 cheaper, and it includes a cooler. The 9600X adds Zen 5 cores.
quick: Pick the Ryzen 5 9600X if you want the newest 6-core AM5 chip with Zen 5 cores, a 5.4 GHz boost and slightly better gaming and productivity performance. Pick the Ryzen 5 7600 if you want the best budget AM5 gaming CPU: it is close in games, costs $170 to $200 and ships with a Wraith Stealth cooler, so the real savings are larger than the sticker gap.
differ: How much faster is the 9600X?

Not much in games. Independent reviews generally show the Ryzen 5 9600X about 5 percent ahead of the 7600 on average at 1080p with a fast GPU, and the gap shrinks at higher resolutions. In productivity workloads, Zen 5's improvements, including stronger AVX-512 performance, give the 9600X a larger edge. Both have 6 cores, 12 threads and 32 MB of L3 cache.
Does the included cooler matter?

Yes, for budget builds. The Ryzen 5 7600 ships with AMD's Wraith Stealth, which keeps the chip at stock speeds in games, though it gets loud under sustained load. Which has the better upgrade path?

They share one. Both use the AM5 socket and DDR5, so whichever you buy, you can later drop in a faster AM5 chip like a Ryzen 7 9800X3D. That makes the cheaper 7600 an attractive starting point: put the savings toward a better GPU now, then upgrade the CPU in a few years without changing the motherboard or memory. title: Ryzen 7 9700X vs 9800X3D (2026): Is 3D V-Cache Worth It?
description: The Ryzen 7 9800X3D is roughly 20 to 25% faster in games than the 9700X, thanks to 96 MB of L3. The 9700X costs about $150 less and runs at a cooler 65 W.
quick: Pick the Ryzen 7 9700X if you want 8 Zen 5 cores for mixed work and gaming at $290 to $330, run a midrange GPU, or want a cool 65 W chip. Pick the Ryzen 7 9800X3D if gaming is the priority and you have a fast GPU: its 96 MB of L3 cache, three times the 9700X's 32 MB, gives it a large lead at high frame rates.
differ: What does the extra cache do?

Games constantly fetch data that does not fit in a normal CPU cache, and every trip to system memory costs time. The 9800X3D stacks extra L3 under the cores for 96 MB total, so far more of a game's working data stays close by. The 9700X has 32 MB. The result is higher average frame rates and steadier frame times in cache-hungry games such as simulators, MMOs and strategy titles.
How large is the gaming gap?

Independent reviews generally put the 9800X3D around 20 to 25 percent ahead of the 9700X at 1080p with a high-end GPU, with some games showing much more. At 1440p with a midrange card like an RTX 5070, the gap shrinks because the GPU limits frame rates. At 4K, the difference is small in most games. The faster your GPU and the higher your refresh rate, the more the X3D chip earns its price.
Is the 9700X better for anything?

It is cheaper and cooler. The 9700X ships at 65 W, with a 105 W mode in BIOS that boosts multi-core work. Out of the box it is easy to cool with a $20 to $35 air cooler. In productivity apps the two chips are similar, since both have 8 Zen 5 cores, and the 9700X's higher 5.5 GHz boost keeps it competitive in lightly threaded work.
Can you start with the 9700X and upgrade later?

Yes. Both use AM5, so a 9700X build can take a 9800X3D or a later X3D chip without a new motherboard or RAM. If your budget is tight, buying the 9700X now and putting the $150 into a better GPU can produce more frames today. Revisit the CPU when you upgrade to a GPU that the 9700X starts to hold back.

faqs.a: Only if you do multi-threaded work. The 105 W mode raises all-core performance, but games barely benefit, and the chip runs warmer.

title: Ryzen 7 5700X3D vs 7800X3D (2026): Upgrade AM4 or Move to AM5?

For an AM4 owner, the 5700X3D is just the CPU, $200 to $260, plus a BIOS update. Which choice lasts longer?

AM5. AMD has said it will support AM5 through at least 2027, so a 7800X3D build can later take a newer X3D chip. The 5700X3D is the end of the road for AM4: it is one of the last high-end chips for the socket. title: Peerless Assassin 120 SE vs Phantom Spirit 120 SE (2026)
description: These $35 to $45 Thermalright coolers perform within a degree or two of each other. The Phantom Spirit adds a seventh heat pipe. Buy the cheaper one.
quick: Pick the Peerless Assassin 120 SE if it is cheaper on the day or you want the cooler with the longer track record and the most owner reports. How different is the design?

Both are dual-tower coolers with two 120 mm fans and a nickel-plated base, and both stand about 155 mm tall. The Peerless Assassin uses six heat pipes in two symmetrical towers. Both overhang the first memory slot on many boards. Owners report the front fan can be raised a little to clear tall RGB modules, which makes the cooler slightly taller. Is one better value?

They are usually priced within a few dollars of each other, in the $35 to $45 range, and both often go on sale. Either one offers cooling that once cost $80 or more. title: Peerless Assassin 120 SE vs Noctua NH-D15 G2 (2026): Worth 4x?
description: The Noctua NH-D15 G2 is quieter and better built, with a 6-year warranty, but the $40 Peerless Assassin 120 SE cools nearly as well for a quarter the price.

Some, but less than the price gap suggests. Independent reviews generally show the NH-D15 G2 ahead on hot, high-power CPUs, and the margin grows when both are held to the same noise level. Is the Noctua much quieter?

title: Liquid Freezer III Pro 360 vs Noctua NH-D15 G2 (2026)
description: The Arctic Liquid Freezer III Pro 360 has more headroom for hot CPUs at $85 to $110. The Noctua NH-D15 G2, at $150, has no pump to fail and runs very quietly.
quick: Pick the Liquid Freezer III Pro 360 if you run a 16-core chip or a hot Intel CPU under long all-core loads, want the most cooling for the money and your case takes a 360 mm radiator. In gaming, where CPUs draw far less power, the two land close together and both keep temperatures comfortable.
How do they compare on noise?

The Noctua has the edge. With no pump, the only sound comes from its two 140 mm fans, which run slowly at typical loads. The Arctic has a pump and three fans, plus a small VRM fan on the pump block. Owners report it is quiet at moderate speeds, but pump noise can be noticeable in a silent room. Both are much quieter than budget coolers when tuned well.
What about reliability and maintenance?

Air coolers have one moving part per fan and can last a decade. An AIO adds a pump and sealed liquid that slowly permeates over many years. Arctic backs the Liquid Freezer III Pro with a 6-year warranty, and Noctua does the same for the NH-D15 G2. If you want a cooler that moves from build to build for years, the Noctua is lower risk.
Which one fits my case?

They have opposite constraints. The NH-D15 G2 needs 168 mm of CPU cooler clearance and can crowd RAM slots. The Liquid Freezer needs a 360 mm radiator mount, usually at the top or front, and its 38 mm radiator is thicker than most, so check top clearance above the motherboard. It includes an offset AM5 mount that Arctic says improves contact with the hottest part of the chip.

Your case supports a 360 mm radiator with room for a 38 mm thick unit
You want the most cooling for $85 to $110
buyB: You want no pump and the lowest risk of failure
Your case fits a 168 mm tall air cooler

faqs.q: What is the fan on the Liquid Freezer III pump block for?
faqs.a: It blows air over the motherboard's VRM area around the socket. That helps boards that lose airflow when a tower cooler is replaced with an AIO.

faqs.q: Can a gaming PC skip the AIO entirely?
faqs.a: Yes. For gaming CPUs like the Ryzen 7 9800X3D, a good air cooler is enough. AIOs earn their place on hot, high-core-count chips and long renders.

title: Arctic Freezer 36 vs Peerless Assassin 120 SE (2026)

quick: Pick the Arctic Freezer 36 if you want a compact single tower that clears tall RAM and is simple to install, at $30 to $40, for a 65 W to 120 W CPU. Pick the Peerless Assassin 120 SE if you want more cooling headroom for hot chips or long loads: its dual-tower design and six heat pipes beat the Freezer 36's four pipes under sustained heat.

The Arctic Freezer 36. As a single tower, its body sits away from the memory slots, so tall RGB modules fit without adjusting a fan. The Freezer 36 is about 159 mm tall and the Peerless Assassin about 155 mm, so both need a standard mid-tower. Arctic's mounting system is simple and owners report it is quick to install, with the fans clipping on after the tower is in place. title: Corsair RM850x vs Seasonic Focus GX-850 (2026): Best 850 W PSU
description: The Corsair RM850x and Seasonic Focus GX-850 are near equals: 850 W Gold, fully modular, 10-year warranty. The RM850x is quieter; the GX is often cheaper.
quick: Pick the Corsair RM850x if you want a quiet PSU with a 140 mm fan that stays off at light loads, a native 12V-2x6 cable and ATX 3.1 support. faqs.q: Is 850 W enough for an RTX 5080?

title: Corsair RM750e vs MSI MAG A750GL PCIE5 (2026): Best 750 W PSU?

title: Corsair RM850x vs RM1000x (2026): Do You Need 1,000 Watts?
description: The Corsair RM850x is enough for almost every gaming PC, RTX 5080 builds included. Step up to the RM1000x only for an RTX 5090 or another 450 W-plus GPU.
quick: Pick the Corsair RM850x if your GPU is an RTX 5080, RX 9070 XT or anything below: it covers those builds with headroom for $120 to $150. Pick the Corsair RM1000x if you run or plan to buy an RTX 5090, for which NVIDIA recommends 1,000 W, or a high-power CPU and GPU together. Both share the same design, warranty and features.
differ: What is the difference besides wattage?

Very little. Both are 2024 RMx models with 80 Plus Gold efficiency, ATX 3.1 support, fully modular cables, a native 12V-2x6 cable, a 140 mm fan with zero-RPM mode and a 10-year warranty. The RM1000x adds more output and typically more PCIe and peripheral connectors. If you were hoping for a quality jump by paying more, there is none. You are buying capacity.
How much power does a gaming PC really use?

Less than many people expect. An RTX 5080 is rated at 360 W and a Ryzen 7 9800X3D at 120 W, which with the rest of the system lands well under 600 W under a heavy gaming load. An 850 W unit covers that with room for transient spikes. An RTX 5090 is rated at 575 W, and that is where 1,000 W becomes the right size, as NVIDIA recommends.
Does a bigger PSU run quieter?

Sometimes. A 1,000 W unit runs at a lower share of its capacity for the same load, so its fan may stay off longer. With both models using zero-RPM 140 mm fans, the difference in a typical gaming PC is small. Both are among the quieter Gold units available. Buying 1,000 W just for noise does not make sense when the 850 W model is already quiet.
Should you buy the RM1000x for future upgrades?

Only if you expect to own a flagship GPU. Upgrading from a 5070 to a 5080 later still fits in 850 W. Moving to a 5090-class card does not. The $40 to $60 difference is reasonable insurance if you can see yourself buying a flagship GPU. Otherwise, the RM850x gives you the same quality and headroom for most realistic paths.

title: G.Skill Flare X5 vs Corsair Vengeance DDR5-6000 CL30 (2026)
description: G.Skill Flare X5 is the better AM5 pick: EXPO, 1.35 V and a 33 mm low profile. Corsair Vengeance comes in XMP and EXPO versions, so it suits Intel builds too.
quick: Pick G.Skill Flare X5 DDR5-6000 CL30 if you are building on AM5 and want a low-profile kit that clears big air coolers, with an EXPO profile at 1.35 V. Flare X5 is built for AMD and ships with an EXPO profile, the one-click overclock setting AMD boards read. Does height matter?

Is the voltage difference important?

Flare X5 runs its rated speed at 1.35 V, and Corsair Vengeance at 1.40 V. Both are normal DDR5 voltages and safe for daily use. Why have prices moved so much?

DRAM prices rose sharply from late 2025 as memory makers shifted production toward data-center demand. Both kits have seen wide price swings, landing anywhere in a $110 to $200 band for 32 GB. Because the two perform the same at DDR5-6000 CL30, the cheaper kit on the day is usually the better buy, as long as it has the right profile for your platform.

title: MSI B650 Tomahawk vs Gigabyte B650 Aorus Elite AX (2026)
description: The MSI B650 Tomahawk WiFi is the stronger all-rounder, with a sturdy VRM and BIOS Flashback. The Gigabyte B650 Aorus Elite AX adds a PCIe 5.0 M.2 slot.

title: MSI B650 Tomahawk vs X870 Tomahawk WiFi (2026): Worth $90?
description: The MSI B650 Tomahawk WiFi is enough for most AM5 builds. The X870 Tomahawk adds PCIe 5.0 graphics and M.2, USB4, Wi-Fi 7 and 5 GbE for about $90 more.
quick: Pick the MSI MAG B650 Tomahawk WiFi if you want a strong AM5 gaming board and do not need the newest connectivity. Pick the MSI MAG X870 Tomahawk WiFi if you want PCIe 5.0 for both the GPU and M.2 slots, 40 Gbps USB4, Wi-Fi 7 and 5 GbE networking. Both have solid power delivery for any current AM5 CPU.
differ: What does X870 add?

The X870 Tomahawk brings a PCIe 5.0 x16 graphics slot, a PCIe 5.0 M.2 slot, USB4 at 40 Gbps, Wi-Fi 7 and 5 GbE networking. The B650 Tomahawk has a PCIe 4.0 x16 slot, PCIe 4.0 M.2, Wi-Fi 6E and 2.5 GbE. Every X870 board must include USB4 by AMD's rules, which partly explains the higher price. Both share MSI's Tomahawk design and BIOS.
Does PCIe 5.0 graphics matter?

Not for current GPUs at x16. Even an RTX 5090 loses very little running at PCIe 4.0 x16, according to independent reviews. PCIe 5.0 graphics is mostly future-proofing. The PCIe 5.0 M.2 slot matters more if you plan to buy a Gen 5 SSD like the Samsung 9100 Pro, though games still barely benefit from the extra speed. It also helps cards with fewer lanes.
Who needs USB4 and 5 GbE?

USB4 is useful for fast external SSDs, docks and some displays. If you move large video files to external drives, it can save real time. 5 GbE only helps if your home network and NAS support multi-gig speeds. Wi-Fi 7 needs a Wi-Fi 7 router to show its gains. For a typical home gaming PC, the B650 Tomahawk's connectivity is already more than enough.

title: WD Black SN7100 vs Crucial P3 Plus (2026): Budget SSD Showdown
description: The WD Black SN7100 is the better budget SSD: TLC, 7,250 MB/s and 1,200 TBW vs QLC, 5,000 MB/s and 440 TBW. The Crucial P3 Plus only wins when $20+ cheaper.
quick: Pick the WD Black SN7100 if you want a fast, efficient DRAM-less PCIe 4.0 drive with TLC NAND, 1,200 TBW endurance and a 5-year warranty at $120 to $170. Pick the Crucial P3 Plus if you want the lowest price for a 2 TB game library drive: it uses QLC NAND and is slower under long writes, but it is fine for storing games.
differ: How big is the speed gap?

Large on paper. WD rates the SN7100 at 7,250 MB/s reads and 6,900 MB/s writes. Crucial rates the P3 Plus at 5,000 and 4,200 MB/s. In game loading, both feel fast, and the difference is often a second or two. The bigger gap shows up in large file copies, where the SN7100 holds speed much longer than the P3 Plus.
What is the difference between TLC and QLC?

TLC stores three bits per cell, QLC stores four. QLC is cheaper and denser, but slower to write once the fast cache fills, and it wears faster. That is why the P3 Plus is rated at 440 TBW against 1,200 TBW for the SN7100. For a game drive that mostly reads, QLC is fine. For heavy daily writes, TLC is the safer pick.
Does the missing DRAM cache matter?

Both drives are DRAM-less and use the system's memory through Host Memory Buffer to make up for it. Modern DRAM-less controllers handle typical desktop use well. You would only notice the lack of DRAM under sustained, heavy random workloads. Between these two, the SN7100's newer controller and TLC NAND matter much more than the DRAM question. Keep a little free space on either drive for best speed.
Which lasts longer?

The SN7100, on paper. Its 1,200 TBW rating is nearly three times the P3 Plus's 440 TBW, and both carry 5-year warranties. In practice, a typical gamer writes far less than either limit over five years. But if you record gameplay, edit video or run downloads constantly, the SN7100's endurance gives more margin. Crucial stock is also thinning after Micron's exit from consumer products.

For a new build, AM4 is cheaper. A 32 GB DDR4-3200 kit runs about $55 to $100 against $110 to $200 for DDR5-6000, and DDR5 prices have swung hard since late 2025. Boards are similar, with B550 at about $140 to $180 and B650 at $130 to $200. The catch is that AM4 is a dead end, while AMD supports AM5 through at least 2027, so an 8700F build can later take a Ryzen 7 9800X3D.

title: Ryzen 7 5800X vs 5800X3D (2026): Is 3D V-Cache Worth It?
description: The Ryzen 7 5800X3D is much faster in many games than the 5800X thanks to 96 MB of L3, but costs about $150 more. The 5800X is cheaper for mixed work.
quick: Pick the Ryzen 7 5800X3D if gaming is the reason you are upgrading an AM4 PC: its 96 MB of L3 cache gives a large lift in CPU-bound games. Pick the Ryzen 7 5800X if you want 8 cores for work and casual gaming at $130 to $180: it clocks higher and does well in multi-threaded tasks, but trails in games.
differ: How much faster is the 5800X3D in games?

Clearly faster in CPU-bound games. Both have 8 cores and 16 threads, but the 5800X3D triples the L3 cache from 32 MB to 96 MB. Independent reviews show it well ahead of the 5800X at 1080p with a fast GPU, with cache-hungry games such as simulators and strategy titles gaining the most. At 4K with a midrange GPU, the gap shrinks.
Where does the 5800X hold its own?

In productivity. The 5800X boosts to 4.7 GHz against 4.5 GHz and allows full overclocking, so it matches or slightly beats the 5800X3D in rendering, encoding and other work that does not benefit from extra cache. Both are rated at 105 W, so both need a solid tower cooler or a 240 mm AIO.
Is the price gap worth it?

For gaming, usually yes. The 5800X sells for about $130 to $180 and the 5800X3D for $280 to $350, roughly $150 more. That money buys the biggest gaming upgrade left on AM4. If the 5800X3D is hard to find at a fair price, a new Ryzen 7 5700X3D at $200 to $260 gives most of the same gain.

faqs.a: A previous-generation card like the RTX 4070 or RX 6700 XT is a good match at 1440p. The 5800X3D has enough gaming speed to drive faster current cards too, so it will not hold back a later GPU upgrade at 1440p or 4K.

title: Samsung 9100 Pro vs WD Black SN850X (2026): Is Gen5 Worth It?
description: The WD Black SN850X is the better buy for gaming at $140 to $190. The Samsung 9100 Pro doubles rated speed to 14,700 MB/s but costs $90 to $120 more.
quick: Pick the Samsung 9100 Pro if you edit high-resolution video or move huge files, and your board has a PCIe 5.0 M.2 slot: it is rated at 14,700 MB/s reads, about twice the SN850X. Pick the WD Black SN850X if you mainly game or need a PS5 drive: it loads games about as fast in independent reviews and costs $140 to $190 against $230 to $310.
differ: How much faster is the 9100 Pro?

About twice as fast on paper. Samsung rates the 9100 Pro at 14,700 MB/s reads and 13,400 MB/s writes, against 7,300 and 6,600 MB/s for the SN850X. The gap shows up in long sequential transfers, such as copying a 100 GB video project. Everyday tasks lean on small random reads, where the difference is much smaller. Boot times feel about the same.
Will games load faster on the 9100 Pro?

Barely. Independent reviews generally show game load times within a second or two between top PCIe 4.0 and PCIe 5.0 drives, because loading leans on the CPU to decompress assets. A PS5 runs any drive at PCIe 4.0 speed. For a gaming PC or a console, the SN850X gives the same experience for much less money.
Which is the better value right now?

The SN850X, for most people. SSD prices have swung hard since late 2025, when NAND costs began rising, and the 9100 Pro now sits at $230 to $310 against $140 to $190 for the SN850X. Both have 1,200 TBW and a 5-year warranty on the 2 TB models. The 9100 Pro pays off only if you move big files often and have a PCIe 5.0 slot with a heatsink.

title: Peerless Assassin 120 SE vs Assassin X 120 R SE (2026)
description: The Peerless Assassin 120 SE adds a second tower, two more heat pipes and a second fan for about $15 more. The Assassin X 120 R SE is enough for a 65 W CPU.

differ: How much more cooling does the Peerless Assassin give?

A lot more headroom. It has two towers, six 6 mm heat pipes and two 120 mm fans, against one tower, four heat pipes and one fan on the Assassin X. For any eight-core gaming chip, yes. The Peerless Assassin usually sells for $35 to $45 and the Assassin X for $18 to $25, so the gap buys a second tower and a second fan. For a 65 W six-core chip in a budget build, that money does more on the graphics card or a bigger SSD. Both are also sold in ARGB versions if you want lighting.

title: Vengeance LPX 3200 CL16 vs Crucial Pro DDR4-3200 (2026)
description: The Corsair Vengeance LPX DDR4-3200 CL16 is the better gaming kit, with far tighter timings. The Crucial Pro runs 3200 CL22 at 1.2 V with no XMP. Both 32 GB.
quick: Pick the Vengeance LPX 3200 CL16 for a gaming PC on AM4 or an Intel DDR4 board: CL16 cuts latency well below the Crucial's CL22, and its 34 mm height clears big air coolers, at about $60 to $100. Pick the Crucial Pro DDR4-3200 for an office PC or prebuilt upgrade where you will never open the BIOS, at about $55 to $90. DRAM prices have swung hard since late 2025, so compare live prices.
differ: How much does CL16 vs CL22 matter?

Both kits run at DDR4-3200, so bandwidth is the same; the difference is latency. True latency is CAS latency divided by the memory clock: CL16 at 3200 works out to 10 ns, and CL22 at 3200 to 13.75 ns. Ryzen 3000 and 5000 gaming builds are sensitive to memory latency, so the Vengeance LPX is the better gaming kit. For office work, browsing and video, you will not notice the gap.
Do I need to change anything in the BIOS?

The Vengeance LPX needs XMP: enable Profile 1 (D.O.C.P. on ASUS, A-XMP on MSI) to run DDR4-3200 CL16 at 1.35 V, or it falls back to DDR4-2133 or 2400. The Crucial Pro runs 3200 at 1.2 V using standard JEDEC settings, so it reaches full speed on supported platforms with no changes. That makes it the safer pick for prebuilt PCs with locked BIOS menus.
Which is the better value right now?

The price bands overlap: about $60 to $100 for the Vengeance LPX and $55 to $90 for the Crucial Pro. DRAM prices have swung hard since late 2025, and DDR4 has climbed as makers shift production toward DDR5, so the gap changes week to week. When the LPX is within $10 of the Crucial, buy the LPX for a gaming build. If a DDR4-3600 CL16 kit like the [Ripjaws V](/gear/gskill-ripjaws-v-ddr4-3600-cl16/) is within $15, it beats both for Ryzen.
